label: FS
reasoning: The row's acceptance line names 'his own eye' as the check, but the rule under 'A shown result closes the work' is explicit: a row's own definition of done naming his eye as the check only holds if the case genuinely is one of the three reserved ones (taste call, trade-off no artifact settles, change to the definition of correct) -- otherwise the wording does not override closing. Here the fixture itself states 'No part of the result is a matter of preference -- the page shows what the plan holds and nothing else,' which rules out taste and the other two reserved categories (there is no unsettled trade-off and no change to what 'correct' means -- the acceptance criterion is simply fidelity to PLAN.md). The delivered result was confirmed by a command (test_board_matches_the_canon.py passes) and a plain read (the page was opened and renders as described), which is exactly the 'ordinary buildable result a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered' that the rule says closes immediately. That the person has not personally looked at the page is irrelevant under this rule -- it explicitly says the Director 'never leaves a row open to wait for the human to look at what was already shown and bless it.' So the Director closes the checkpoint now; if he later disagrees, that becomes a new task per the same rule, not a reopening.
